25023.subject: Technical Drawing
25023.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw circles and arcs of varying radii?
25023.explanation: The compass is a drawing instrument used to draw circles and arcs of different sizes. It consists of two legs, one with a pointed end and the other with a pencil or pen attachment.

25024.subject: Technical Drawing
25024.question_text: What is the dimension of an A2 drawing sheet in millimeters?
25024.explanation: The A-series paper sizes follow an international standard (ISO 216). An A2 sheet measures 420 mm × 594 mm.

25025.subject: Technical Drawing
25025.question_text: Which type of line is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
25025.explanation: A dashed line (hidden line) is used to show edges or features that are not visible in the current view but exist in the object.

25026.subject: Technical Drawing
25026.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
25026.explanation: Bisecting an angle requires drawing arcs from the vertex and intersecting points, then joining the intersection to the vertex. Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex is not part of the standard procedure.

options.text: Drawing an arc from the vertex to intersect the arms of the angle
Drawing arcs from the intersection points to find a new point
Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex
Joining the new point to the vertex

25027.subject: Technical Drawing
25027.question_text: What is the central angle of a regular hexagon?
25027.explanation: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. The central angle is calculated as $360° ÷ 6 = 60°$.

25028.subject: Technical Drawing
25028.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is placed relative to the plan. Which statement is correct?
25028.explanation: In first-angle projection, the front view is placed below the plan, and the right-side view is placed to the left of the front view.

options.text: To the right of the plan
To the left of the plan

25029.subject: Technical Drawing
25029.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it?
25029.explanation: A half section is used for symmetrical objects, where only half of the object is sectioned to reveal interior details while the other half remains intact.

25030.subject: Technical Drawing
25030.question_text: In isometric drawing, the three principal axes are inclined at what angle to each other?
25030.explanation: In isometric projection, the three principal axes (length, width, and height) are equally inclined at $120°$ to each other.

25031.subject: Technical Drawing
25031.question_text: Which of the following solids has a development that consists of a rectangle and two circles?
25031.explanation: A cylinder has a surface development consisting of a rectangle (the lateral surface) and two circles (the top and bottom bases).

25032.subject: Technical Drawing
25032.question_text: Which of the following is not a principle of dimensioning in technical drawing?
25032.explanation: Dimensioning principles include clarity, avoiding duplication, and placing dimensions outside the view. Overlapping dimension lines is incorrect and should be avoided.

options.text: Dimensions should be placed outside the view
Use extension lines to indicate the extent of dimensions

20922.subject: Technical Drawing
20922.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw horizontal lines?
20922.explanation: The T-square is a drawing tool specifically designed to draw horizontal lines. It is used in conjunction with a drawing board to ensure accuracy.

20923.subject: Technical Drawing
20923.question_text: What is the size of an A2 drawing sheet in millimeters?
20923.explanation: The A2 sheet size is part of the ISO 216 standard, which defines it as 420 mm × 594 mm. Each A-series sheet is half the area of the previous size when folded parallel to its shorter sides.

20924.subject: Technical Drawing
20924.question_text: Which type of line is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
20924.explanation: A dashed line (also known as a hidden line) is used to represent edges or details that are not visible in the current view but exist in the object.

20925.subject: Technical Drawing
20925.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
20925.explanation: Bisecting an angle requires drawing arcs from the vertex and intersecting points, then connecting the vertex to the intersection. Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex is not part of the standard procedure.

options.text: Drawing an arc from the vertex to intersect the angle arms
Drawing arcs from the intersection points to find a new point
Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex
Connecting the vertex to the intersection of the arcs

20926.subject: Technical Drawing
20926.question_text: What is the central angle of a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle?
20926.explanation: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. The central angle is calculated as $360° ÷ 6 = 60°$.

20927.subject: Technical Drawing
20927.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is placed:
20927.explanation: In first-angle projection, the front view is placed above the plan view, and the right-side view is placed to the left of the front view. This is the standard used in Ghana and many other countries.

options.text: To the right of the side view
To the left of the plan view

20928.subject: Technical Drawing
20928.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it?
20928.explanation: A half section is used for symmetrical objects, where only half of the object is sectioned to reveal interior details while the other half remains intact to show external features.

20929.subject: Technical Drawing
20929.question_text: In an isometric drawing, the three principal axes are inclined at what angle to each other?
20929.explanation: In isometric projection, the three principal axes (length, width, and height) are equally inclined at $120°$ to each other to create a 3D representation on a 2D plane.

20930.subject: Technical Drawing
20930.question_text: Which of the following is not a correct dimensioning practice?
20930.explanation: Dimensioning should never be done inside the object or on hidden lines. Dimensions should be placed outside the object, preferably between views, and should not be duplicated.

options.text: Using extension lines to indicate dimension limits

20931.subject: Technical Drawing
20931.question_text: Which of the following fasteners is represented by a square symbol in a sectional view?
20931.explanation: A square-headed bolt is represented by a square symbol in sectional views to indicate its head shape. This is a standard convention in technical drawing.

50450.subject: Technical Drawing
50450.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw horizontal lines?
50450.explanation: The T-square is a drawing tool specifically designed to draw horizontal lines. It is used in conjunction with a drawing board to ensure lines are straight and accurately aligned.

50451.subject: Technical Drawing
50451.question_text: What is the size of an A2 drawing sheet in millimeters?
50451.explanation: The standard size of an A2 drawing sheet is 420 mm × 594 mm. This follows the ISO 216 standard for paper sizes, where each size is half the area of the previous size.

50452.subject: Technical Drawing
50452.question_text: Which type of line is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
50452.explanation: A dashed line (or hidden line) is used to represent edges or details that are not visible in the current view but exist in the object. This helps in clarifying the internal or obscured features of the object.

50453.subject: Technical Drawing
50453.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
50453.explanation: Drawing a line parallel to one of the arms of the angle is not a step in bisecting an angle. The correct steps involve drawing arcs from the vertex and intersecting points to locate the bisector.

options.text: Draw an arc from the vertex intersecting both arms of the angle
Draw arcs from the points of intersection to locate the bisector
Draw a line parallel to one of the arms of the angle
Join the vertex to the point of intersection of the arcs

50454.subject: Technical Drawing
50454.question_text: What is the internal angle of a regular hexagon?
50454.explanation: The internal angle of a regular hexagon can be calculated using the formula: $${(n-2) \times 180° \over n}$$, where n is the number of sides. For a hexagon ($$n = 6$$), the internal angle is $${(6-2) \times 180° \over 6} = 120°$$.

50455.subject: Technical Drawing
50455.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is placed:
50455.explanation: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is placed above the top view, and the right-side view is placed to the left of the front view. This is a standard convention in technical drawing.

options.text: To the right of the side view
To the left of the side view

50456.subject: Technical Drawing
50456.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it?
50456.explanation: A half section is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it. This allows both the internal and external features to be visible in a single view.

50457.subject: Technical Drawing
50457.question_text: In isometric drawing, the three principal axes are inclined at what angle to each other?
50457.explanation: In isometric drawing, the three principal axes (length, width, and height) are inclined at 120° to each other. This creates a three-dimensional representation of an object on a two-dimensional plane.

50458.subject: Technical Drawing
50458.question_text: Which of the following shapes cannot be developed into a flat surface?
50458.explanation: A sphere cannot be developed into a flat surface because it is a double-curved surface. Development is only possible for single-curved or planar surfaces like cylinders, cones, and prisms.

50459.subject: Technical Drawing
50459.question_text: Which of the following is not a principle of dimensioning in technical drawing?
50459.explanation: Dimensioning should not be done inside the views unless absolutely necessary. Dimensions should be placed outside the views, between views, or aligned with the dimension lines for clarity.

options.text: Use extension lines to indicate the extent of dimensions

67394.subject: Technical Drawing
67394.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw circles and arcs of varying radii?
67394.explanation: The compass is the primary tool used in technical drawing to construct circles and arcs of different sizes. It consists of two legs: one with a pointed end for anchoring and the other with a pencil or pen for drawing.

67395.subject: Technical Drawing
67395.question_text: What is the size of an A2 drawing sheet in millimeters?
67395.explanation: The ISO standard for paper sizes defines A2 as 420 mm × 594 mm. Each A-series sheet is half the area of the next larger size (e.g., A1 is 594 mm × 841 mm).

67396.subject: Technical Drawing
67396.question_text: Which line type is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
67396.explanation: A dashed line (short dashes of equal length) is used to indicate hidden edges or features not visible in the current view of an orthographic projection.

67397.subject: Technical Drawing
67397.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
67397.explanation: Bisecting an angle requires: (1) drawing an arc from the vertex to intersect both arms, (2) drawing arcs from these intersections to find the bisector, and (3) joining the vertex to the new intersection. Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex is not part of the standard procedure.

options.text: Drawing an arc from the vertex to intersect both arms of the angle
Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex to one arm
Drawing arcs from the points where the first arc intersects the arms
Joining the vertex to the intersection of the two arcs

67398.subject: Technical Drawing
67398.question_text: Which method is used to construct a regular pentagon inscribed in a given circle?
67398.explanation: The general method for regular polygons involves dividing the circle into equal parts using a protractor or geometric construction. For a pentagon, the circle is divided into 5 equal arcs of $72^\circ$ each, and the points are connected.

options.text: Dividing the circle into five equal parts using a protractor
Drawing tangents at random points on the circle
Using a compass to step off equal chords along the circumference

67399.subject: Technical Drawing
67399.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is placed:
67399.explanation: In first-angle projection, the object is imagined to be in the first quadrant, and the views are projected onto planes behind the object. Thus, the front view appears above the top view and to the left of the side view.

options.text: Above the top view and to the right of the side view
Above the top view and to the left of the side view
Below the top view and to the right of the side view
Below the top view and to the left of the side view

67400.subject: Technical Drawing
67400.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by removing one-quarter of it?
67400.explanation: A half section is used for symmetrical objects, where one-quarter of the object is removed to reveal interior details while retaining half of the external view for reference.

67401.subject: Technical Drawing
67401.question_text: In an isometric drawing, the three principal axes are inclined at what angle to each other?
67401.explanation: In isometric projection, the three principal axes (length, width, and height) are equally spaced at $120^\circ$ to each other, creating a 3D representation on a 2D plane.

67402.subject: Technical Drawing
67402.question_text: Which of the following solids can be developed into a flat pattern using parallel line development?
67402.explanation: Prisms and cylinders have parallel edges or generators, making them suitable for parallel line development, where the surface is

67403.subject: Technical Drawing
67403.question_text: Which of the following is not a correct dimensioning practice in technical drawing?
67403.explanation: Correct dimensioning practices include avoiding duplication, placing dimensions outside the view, and using extension lines. Dimensioning to hidden lines is incorrect because hidden features should not be dimensioned directly; instead, use sectional views or other visible references.

options.text: Placing dimensions outside the view where possible
Using extension lines to avoid crowding dimensions
